title: Muxed address from ID 2^53+1 passed as a native number: exact or refused
why: 2^53+1 is a valid uint64 but not a safe IEEE-754 double: a JavaScript number literal is already 9007199254740992 before the SDK sees it, so an SDK must encode the exact ID or refuse the number.
notes: Built by xdrcheck-corpus synth from corpus/recipes/cap-0027/api-muxed-account-id-encoding.id-2-pow-53-plus-1-number.json. Origin: probe vector 2m1, in evidence/sdk-matrix/vectors/vectors.json, executed in every probe column (evidence/sdk-matrix). Exact or refuse: either the M-address of ID 9007199254740993 (SEP-0023: key || id) and the MuxedAccount XDR (KEY_TYPE_MUXED_ED25519, id, key), or a refusal. Languages with exact 64-bit integers get the exact value. Expected values were computed from the XDR definitions, the CAP or SEP text and the stellar-core rule cited under related, with an independent encoder; no SDK output was used.
